Garlic Butter Spaghetti 🔥 Quick, easy, and dangerously good. Buttery garlic heaven with a hint of spice… Pro Tip: Level it up with chicken, shrimp, or tofu 🫡 Ingredients: -2 shallots, thinly sliced -5 garlic cloves, minced -2 tbsp chili crisp -1 cup of cream or coconut milk, room temperature -1 tbsp soy sauce, optional -1/2 cup fresh Parmesan cheese, grated -8 oz (225g) pasta of your choice -2 tbsp butter -1 tbsp olive oil -Seasonings (1 tsp each): paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper, oregano 1. Slice your shallots nice and thin and measure out your seasonings. Bring your cream or coconut milk to room temp so it blends in smoothly later. 2. Heat 2 tbsp butter + 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Add the shallots and sauté for 8–10 minutes until soft and starting to turn golden. 3. While the shallots are doing their thing, bring a big pot of salted water to a boil and cook your pasta until al dente. Drain, but save some pasta water… it’s liquid gold. Seriously, don’t you dare dump it. Italians everywhere are watching. 4. Once the shallots are soft and sweet, stir in your minced garlic (fresh garlic only - if you pull out that jarred stuff, the FBI will be at your door in minutes 😅) and all the seasonings. Let them bloom for about a minute, then add the chili crisp and give it another quick sauté. 5. Pour in the cream (or coconut milk), stir in the soy sauce if using, and let it simmer for a few minutes to thicken. Add in the grated Parmesan and stir. 6. Toss your pasta in the sauce until fully coated, adding splashes of reserved pasta water as needed to get that perfect silky consistency. 7. Serve hot with an extra spoonful of chili crisp on top for a little heat and a sprinkle of Parmesan and parsley if you’re feelin’ fancy. #dinnerideas #recipe #cookingathometiktoktv #pasta

30-Minute Garlic Butter Steak Bites & Potatoes 🥩🥔🧄 If you need a quick and easy dinner idea, you have to try these garlic butter steak bites and potatoes! The potatoes are perfectly seasoned and crispy, and the steak is juicy, tender, and tossed in the most delicious garlic butter. And the best part? You can have dinner on the table in about 30 minutes! 🤤 RECIPE BELOW ⬇️  Potatoes: * 4 russet potatoes, diced * 2 tbsp olive oil * 1 tsp each: salt, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika & Italian seasoning * ½ tsp black pepper Steak: * 1½ lbs sirloin tip steak, cubed * 1 tsp olive oil * 1–2 tsp Montreal steak seasoning * 1 tbsp oil for cooking * 2 tbsp butter * 3 cloves garlic, minced * Fresh parsley Instructions 👩🏽‍🍳 1. Wash, peel, and dice your potatoes. Toss with olive oil and seasonings. Salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and Italian seasoning. Y’all know I don’t measure. I just season until my ancestors tell me to stop! 😂 2. Air fry at 400°F for 20–25 minutes, shaking halfway through, until crispy. You can also bake at 425°F for 25–30 minutes or pan-fry! 3. While those cook, cut your steak into bite-sized pieces and toss with a little olive oil and steak seasoning. I used Montreal, but use your favorite! 4. Get your skillet nice and hot! Add a little oil and sear steak for about 2 minutes per side until browned. Cast iron works best, but any skillet will do! 5. Reduce heat, scoot steak to the edges, and add butter and garlic. Cook for 30–60 seconds until fragrant, then toss everything in that garlic butter. 6. Turn off the heat, add your crispy potatoes, gently mix, and top with fresh parsley! Serve with cheesy rice, mac and cheese, asparagus, or whatever your heart desires! ❤️ Save this for your next easy weeknight dinner! 🔖 #GarlicButterSteakBites #SteakAndPotatoes #30MinuteMeals #EasyDinnerIdeas #WeeknightDinners

GROUND BEEF BULGOGI A quick, savory Korean‑inspired beef bowl that’s perfect for weeknights. INGREDIENTS Main 1 lb ground beef 1 onion, sliced 1 tbsp minced garlic Oil, for cooking Sesame oil, for finishing Sesame seeds, garnish Chopped scallion, garnish Kimchi or radish kimchi, for serving Sauce 2 tbsp brown sugar 2 tbsp mirin 4 tbsp soy sauce (low sodium preferred) 1 tbsp Korean plum syrup* *Sub: 1 tbsp water + 1 tsp apple cider vinegar INSTRUCTIONS 1. Peel and slice the onion; set aside. 2. Combine brown sugar, mirin, soy sauce, and plum syrup (or substitute). Mix well and set aside. 3. Heat a little oil in a pan. Add sliced onions and cook for 1 minute. Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. 4. Add ground beef and break it into small pieces. Once the beef is about 30% cooked, pour in the sauce. Let it simmer until the sauce reduces and evaporates — stir occasionally. (This part takes a little time, but it’s worth it.) 5. Drizzle with sesame oil and give it a final mix. 6. Assemble your bowl with rice, scallions, sesame seeds, and kimchi/ veggie of choice. Enjoy!

🥩🍲 Slow Cooker Garlic Butter Beef & Onion Gravy This tender, juicy slow-cooked beef is the ultimate comfort food! Thick, beautifully browned pieces of beef simmer low and slow in a rich, savory garlic butter gravy with sweet caramelized onions. Every piece is coated in a delicious, glossy sauce that makes this dish absolutely irresistible. The slow cooking process allows the beef to soak up all those incredible flavors until it's fork-tender and incredibly juicy. It's the kind of hearty, homemade dinner that fills the kitchen with an amazing aroma and brings everyone to the table. ❤️ 🥘 Ingredients 2 lbs beef chuck steak or boneless beef roast, sliced into thick pieces 2 large onions, sliced 4 cloves garlic, minced 3 tbsp butter 2 cups beef broth 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce 1 tbsp soy sauce 1 tbsp tomato paste 1 tsp paprika 1 tsp garlic powder ½ tsp black pepper Salt to taste 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water (optional) 👩‍🍳 Instructions Season the beef with salt, black pepper, paprika, and garlic powder. Heat a skillet with a little oil and sear the beef on both sides until nicely browned. Place sliced onions and minced garlic in the slow cooker. Arrange the browned beef over the onions. Mix beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, and tomato paste. Pour over the beef. Add butter on top, cover, and cook on LOW for 7–8 hours or HIGH for 4–5 hours, until fork-tender. If desired, thicken the gravy with the cornstarch mixture during the final 20–30 minutes. Spoon that rich, flavorful onion gravy over the beef and serve hot! 😍 Perfect with creamy mashed potatoes, buttery rice, or warm dinner rolls to soak up every drop of that delicious gravy! Coming very soon, so follow my page so you don’t miss it Ingredients • 5 lb Yukon gold potatoes • 16 oz cream cheese, softened • ⅓ cup sour cream • ½ cup milk • 1 stick butter, softened, plus extra slices for topping • 1 tsp black pepper • 2 tsp salt • Paprika, for topping • 1 bunch fresh chives, chopped Instructions 1. Set out the cream cheese and butter to soften. Preheat the oven to 400°F. 2. Boiling Method: Peel the potatoes and cut into evenly sized chunks. Place in a large pot, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer and cook for 15–20 minutes, or until fork-tender. 3. Instant Pot Method (Alternative): Add 1 cup of water to the Instant Pot and place the trivet inside. Add the whole, unpeeled potatoes. Pressure cook on high for 14 minutes, then allow a 10-minute natural pressure release before releasing the remaining pressure. Carefully remove, cool slightly, and peel. Cook in batches if necessary. 4. Transfer cooked potatoes to a large mixing bowl. Add cream cheese, sour cream, milk, butter, salt, and pepper. 5. Use a hand mixer or stand mixer to mix until smooth and creamy, being careful not to overmix. 6. Transfer to a greased 9×13-inch baking dish and spread evenly. 7. Sprinkle paprika over the top and add a few thin slices of butter. 8. Cover tightly with aluminum foil. 9. Bake at 400°F for 60 minutes, or until heated through. 10. Remove the foil during the final 5 minutes to lightly brown the top. 11. Sprinkle the freshly chopped chives over the top before serving. Make-Ahead Instructions 1. Prepare the mashed potatoes following steps 1–8 above, using either cooking method. Wait to preheat the oven until you’re ready to bake. 2. Cover tightly with foil and refrigerate for up to 2 days. 3. Remove from the refrigerator 30 minutes before baking. 4. Preheat oven to 400°F. 5. Bake covered for approximately 60 minutes, until hot in the center. 6. Remove foil for the final 5 minutes to lightly brown the top. 7. Sprinkle with the chopped chives before serving. #mashedpotatoes #EasyRecipe

FRY BREAD TACOS This dinner took me right back to being a little kid, going to Pow Wow’s in the summer and eating fry bread. You could get it sweet with powdered sugar and honey, or savory, and fry bread tacos were one of my favorites. I remember beans on them too, but I kept mine simple because one of my kids doesn’t like beans. Ground beef, lettuce, cheese, homemade pico, and sour cream. Add hot sauce, add beans, add whatever you want. You’re the one eating it! Makes 8 fry bread tacos FRY BREAD • 3 cups all-purpose flour • 2 teaspoons baking powder • 1 teaspoon salt • Approximately 1 cup warm water, adding more as needed • Olive oil or your preferred frying oil TACO MEAT • 2 pounds ground beef • 1 medium onion, grated • 3 cloves garlic, grated • 1½ cups water • 1½ teaspoons Better Than Bouillon, any flavor you like. I used garlic. • 6 tablespoons Brooke’s Zesty Lime Taco Seasoning OR 2 packets taco seasoning TOPPINGS • Shredded lettuce • Shredded cheese • Pico de gallo • Sour cream • Hot sauce, optional 1. Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt. Gradually add the warm water until the dough comes together. You want it soft and workable, without being crumbly or sticky. Add a little more water if it’s dry or a little flour if it’s too sticky. 2. Gently knead into a ball. Divide in half, then halve those pieces, then halve again to make 8 pieces. Flatten each piece between two sheets of parchment paper. Keep covered and let rest while you make the taco meat. 3. Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, adding the grated onion and garlic as it cooks. Cook until the beef is browned and the onion and garlic are tender. Drain excess grease if needed. 4. Stir in the water, Better Than Bouillon, and taco seasoning. Simmer uncovered until the excess liquid cooks off and the meat is nice and saucy without being watery. 5. Add enough oil to a separate skillet to generously cover the bottom with no dry spots. Heat over medium heat until a small piece of dough sizzles when added. 6. Carefully place the flattened dough in the hot oil, working in batches. Fry about 1–2 minutes per side until puffed and golden brown. When the bottom and edges are golden, flip and cook the other side. Adjust the heat as needed. 7. Drain on paper towels, then pile on the taco meat and your toppings. GALBI JJIM- Korean braised short ribs  Ingredients * 3.5 pounds boneless short ribs, cut into 2-3” cubes  * 8 ounces Korean radish mu, cut into large chunks * 2 medium carrots cut into large chunks * 4 shiitake mushrooms, soaked till softened and quartered  Braising liquid: * 1/2 medium Korean Asian pear or 1 small apple chopped * 1/2 medium onion diced  * 5 plump garlic cloves * 1 inch ginger piece * 1/2 cup tamari or soy sauce  * 2 tbsp rice wine vinegar  * 2 tbsp coconut sugar or white sugar  * 2 tbsp honey  * 2 tbsp sesame oil * pepper to taste Garnish: * Chopped green onions * Roasted sesame seeds - Lightly season your cubed meat with salt.  - Heat up a large Dutch oven and drop a tbsp of tallow. - Sear your cubed meat in batches to get a good crusty sear on all sides.  - Add all seared meat back into the Dutch oven.  - Toss all braising ingredients into a blender and blend.  - Pour braising liquid on top of your beef and bring to a boil. Lid on, rolling simmer on medium heat for 30 minutes. - Open the lid and add your radish, carrots and mushrooms. Give it a good stir to allow the veggies to get soaked in the braising liquid. - Lid back on and braise for another 30 minutes. - Lid off, garnish with green onions and sesame seeds, serve along side rice and kimchi!

It cooks effortlessly in the slow cooker! INGREDIENTS: - 1 1/2 lbs chicken breasts, diced - 2 lbs baby potatoes, halved or quartered - 1 1/2 cups corn kernels (fresh, frozen, or drained canned) - 1 can (10.5 oz) cream of chicken soup - 1/4 cup milk or chicken broth - 1 tsp garlic powder - 1/2 tsp salt - 1/2 tsp black pepper - 1 1/2 cups shredded cheddar cheese - 6 slices bacon, cooked and crumbled - 2 tbsp chopped parsley INSTRUCTIONS: 1. Place the diced chicken and baby potatoes into the slow cooker. Season with garlic powder, salt, and pepper. 2. Whisk the cream of chicken soup with the milk or broth, then pour it over the chicken and potatoes. 3. Sprinkle the corn kernels over the top. 4. Sprinkle the cheddar cheese and crispy bacon bits over everything. 5. Put the lid on and cook on low for 4-5 hours or on high for 2-3 hours, until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are tender. 6. Shred the chicken with two forks, stir everything together, sprinkle with parsley, and serve hot straight from the slow cooker.
